Loading Libraries

library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))

Loading Data

Each row is a course entry, not a unique course or an individual student. Repeated course entries are retained. Mean GPA below is the unweighted mean of course average GPAs, so each course entry receives equal weight. Missing values are excluded from the relevant numerical summaries and plots, but retained in entry counts.

# Data from reddit user austingwalters:
# https://www.reddit.com/r/udub/comments/4e6kxl/i_made_a_website_that_shows_grade_distributions/
# Dataset and FOIA information:
# https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fo/8lbyazjlt5jmv86jvvs06/AGtgMaWeyZtZuS2fSYLYn_4?dl=0&e=1&rlkey=1sg7t372nhslxogwjl3e9lt9t
uw_grades_original_df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kylethayer/Info-201-au-24-datasets/refs/heads/main/UW-Seattle_20110-20161-Course-Grade-Data_2016-04-06.csv", check.names = FALSE)

uw_grades_df <- uw_grades_original_df |>
  mutate(
    Program_Abv = str_split_i(Course_Number, " ", 1),
    Course_Number_Num = as.integer(str_extract(Course_Number, "\\d+")),
    Term_Season = str_extract(Term, "Autumn|Spring|Summer|Winter")
  )

Overall Grade Distribution Summary

overall_summary <- uw_grades_df |>
  summarise(
    course_entries = n(),
    mean_gpa = mean(Average_GPA, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_students = mean(Student_Count, na.rm = TRUE),
    minimum_course_number = min(Course_Number_Num, na.rm = TRUE),
    maximum_course_number = max(Course_Number_Num, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
knitr::kable(overall_summary, digits = 2,
             col.names = c("Course entries", "Mean course GPA", "Mean students",
                           "Minimum course number", "Maximum course number"))
Course entries Mean course GPA Mean students Minimum course number Maximum course number
39242 3.41 45.38 100 750 
sum(is.na(uw_grades_df$Average_GPA))
[1] 1
ggplot(uw_grades_df, aes(x = Average_GPA)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.1, boundary = 0.05,
                 fill = "#287C8E", color = "white", na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(1.5, 4.1), breaks = seq(1.5, 4, 0.5)) +
  labs(title = "Grade façade: all courses",
       x = "Average course GPA", y = "Number of course entries")
ggplot(uw_grades_df, aes(x = Student_Count, y = Average_GPA)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.18, size = 1.2, color = "#56428C", na.rm = TRUE) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 750), ylim = c(1.5, 4.1)) +
  labs(title = "Size and GPA façade: all courses",
       x = "Number of students", y = "Average course GPA")

The dataset contains 39242 course entries. The average of course average GPAs is 3.41, and the average enrollment is 45.38 students. Course numbers range from 100 to 750. One entry has a missing average GPA, so the GPA mean and GPA plots use 39,241 entries. The histogram is concentrated in the 3.0–4.0 range, with its highest bar around 3.5 and a longer tail toward lower GPAs. The scatterplot contains many more small classes than very large classes. Small classes span a wide GPA range, and some large classes also have high GPAs, so enrollment alone does not determine course GPA. Horizontal bands reflect the one-decimal precision of the reported GPAs.

Comparison #1: INFO versus MATH

This comparison uses the program abbreviations produced by the required data processing code. Both scatterplots use the same axis limits; both histograms use the same bin width and axis limits. Histogram heights are counts, so the different numbers of entries must be considered when comparing the programs.

info_df <- uw_grades_df |> filter(Program_Abv == "INFO")
math_df <- uw_grades_df |> filter(Program_Abv == "MATH")

info_summary <- info_df |>
  summarise(course_entries = n(),
            mean_gpa = mean(Average_GPA, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean_students = mean(Student_Count, na.rm = TRUE),
            median_gpa = median(Average_GPA, na.rm = TRUE))
math_summary <- math_df |>
  summarise(course_entries = n(),
            mean_gpa = mean(Average_GPA, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean_students = mean(Student_Count, na.rm = TRUE),
            median_gpa = median(Average_GPA, na.rm = TRUE))

program_summary <- bind_rows(INFO = info_summary, MATH = math_summary, .id = "Program")
knitr::kable(program_summary, digits = 2,
             col.names = c("Program", "Course entries", "Mean course GPA",
                           "Mean students", "Median course GPA"))
Program Course entries Mean course GPA Mean students Median course GPA
INFO 288 3.56 53.01 3.6
MATH 1843 2.98 57.70 3.0 
program_hist_max <- 1.1 * max(table(info_df$Average_GPA), table(math_df$Average_GPA))

INFO

ggplot(info_df, aes(x = Average_GPA)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.1, boundary = 0.05,
                 fill = "#287C8E", color = "white", na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(1.5, 4.1), breaks = seq(1.5, 4, 0.5)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, program_hist_max)) +
  labs(title = "Grade façade: INFO courses",
       x = "Average course GPA", y = "Number of course entries")
ggplot(info_df, aes(x = Student_Count, y = Average_GPA)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.18, size = 1.2, color = "#56428C", na.rm = TRUE) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 250), ylim = c(1.5, 4.1)) +
  labs(title = "Size and GPA façade: INFO courses",
       x = "Number of students", y = "Average course GPA")

MATH

ggplot(math_df, aes(x = Average_GPA)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.1, boundary = 0.05,
                 fill = "#287C8E", color = "white", na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(1.5, 4.1), breaks = seq(1.5, 4, 0.5)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, program_hist_max)) +
  labs(title = "Grade façade: MATH courses",
       x = "Average course GPA", y = "Number of course entries")
ggplot(math_df, aes(x = Student_Count, y = Average_GPA)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.18, size = 1.2, color = "#56428C", na.rm = TRUE) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 250), ylim = c(1.5, 4.1)) +
  labs(title = "Size and GPA façade: MATH courses",
       x = "Number of students", y = "Average course GPA")

Program comparison observations

INFO contains 288 entries, with a mean course GPA of 3.56, a mean enrollment of 53.01 students, and a median course GPA of 3.60. MATH contains 1843 entries, with a mean course GPA of 2.98, a mean enrollment of 57.70 students, and a median course GPA of 3.00.

INFO’s mean course GPA is approximately 0.58 GPA points higher. The INFO histogram is concentrated at higher GPAs, while the MATH histogram extends farther into lower GPAs. The scatterplots likewise show INFO entries mostly in a higher GPA band; MATH shows a wider vertical spread and some larger classes. Both programs have overlapping GPAs and broadly similar average enrollments. The much taller MATH histogram bars partly reflect its larger number of entries, not simply a stronger concentration. These descriptive differences do not establish that one program is easier: course levels, students, instructors, and grading practices may differ.

Comparison #2: Course numbers 100–299 versus 300–499

The second comparison combines programs and compares two nonoverlapping course number ranges. Courses numbered 500 or above are excluded from this comparison. As in Comparison #1, the plots share axis limits within each plot type.

lower_df <- uw_grades_df |>
  filter(Course_Number_Num >= 100, Course_Number_Num < 300)
upper_df <- uw_grades_df |>
  filter(Course_Number_Num >= 300, Course_Number_Num < 500)

lower_summary <- lower_df |>
  summarise(course_entries = n(),
            mean_gpa = mean(Average_GPA, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean_students = mean(Student_Count, na.rm = TRUE),
            median_gpa = median(Average_GPA, na.rm = TRUE))
upper_summary <- upper_df |>
  summarise(course_entries = n(),
            mean_gpa = mean(Average_GPA, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean_students = mean(Student_Count, na.rm = TRUE),
            median_gpa = median(Average_GPA, na.rm = TRUE))

level_summary <- bind_rows("100–299" = lower_summary, "300–499" = upper_summary,
                           .id = "Course range")
knitr::kable(level_summary, digits = 2,
             col.names = c("Course range", "Course entries", "Mean course GPA",
                           "Mean students", "Median course GPA"))
Course range Course entries Mean course GPA Mean students Median course GPA
100–299 11964 3.31 66.25 3.3
300–499 17502 3.35 39.77 3.4 
level_hist_max <- 1.1 * max(table(lower_df$Average_GPA), table(upper_df$Average_GPA))

Course numbers 100–299

ggplot(lower_df, aes(x = Average_GPA)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.1, boundary = 0.05,
                 fill = "#287C8E", color = "white", na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(1.5, 4.1), breaks = seq(1.5, 4, 0.5)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, level_hist_max)) +
  labs(title = "Grade façade: courses 100–299",
       x = "Average course GPA", y = "Number of course entries")
ggplot(lower_df, aes(x = Student_Count, y = Average_GPA)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.18, size = 1.2, color = "#56428C", na.rm = TRUE) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 750), ylim = c(1.5, 4.1)) +
  labs(title = "Size and GPA façade: courses 100–299",
       x = "Number of students", y = "Average course GPA")

Course numbers 300–499

ggplot(upper_df, aes(x = Average_GPA)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.1, boundary = 0.05,
                 fill = "#287C8E", color = "white", na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(1.5, 4.1), breaks = seq(1.5, 4, 0.5)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, level_hist_max)) +
  labs(title = "Grade façade: courses 300–499",
       x = "Average course GPA", y = "Number of course entries")
ggplot(upper_df, aes(x = Student_Count, y = Average_GPA)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.18, size = 1.2, color = "#56428C", na.rm = TRUE) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 750), ylim = c(1.5, 4.1)) +
  labs(title = "Size and GPA façade: courses 300–499",
       x = "Number of students", y = "Average course GPA")

Course number comparison observations

Courses numbered 100–299 include 11964 entries, with a mean course GPA of 3.31, a mean enrollment of 66.25 students, and a median course GPA of 3.30. Courses numbered 300–499 include 17502 entries, with a mean course GPA of 3.35, a mean enrollment of 39.77 students, and a median course GPA of 3.40.

The mean GPA differs by only 0.04 points, with the higher-numbered group slightly higher. The histograms overlap substantially in GPA range and are both concentrated toward the upper end of the scale. A more pronounced difference is enrollment: the mean for the 100–299 group is 26.48 students greater. Its scatterplot shows more entries extending into large class sizes, while the 300–499 group is more concentrated at small enrollments, although both contain large-class outliers. Neither scatterplot shows a one-to-one relationship between class size and GPA. Because this comparison mixes programs and instructors, it does not isolate a causal effect of course level on grades.
